FEDERAL POWER COMMISSION REGIONAL OFFICE
819 Taylor Street Fort Worth, Texas 76102 April 12, 1976
In reply refer to:
Mr. Gordon A. Walhood, P. E. Chief, Engineering Division Ft. Worth District, Corps of Engineers P. O. Box 17300 Fort Worth, Texas 76102
Dear Mr. Walhood:
This is in reply to your March 16, 1976, letter (SWFED-PR) concerning the Federal Power Commission's land use policies or any environmental impact areas affected by the proposed addition of hydroelectric generating facilities at the Amistad Lake Project. The Federal Power Commission's land use policies are confined to lands within the project boundaries at water resources projects licensed by the Commission. A normal condition of the license is that adequate lands be provided around the reservoir for recreation purposes. The addition to the Amistad Project will not affect the land use policies of the Commission.
The Maverick County Water Control and Improvement District No. 1 project located downstream from Amistad, near Eagle Pass, Texas, is licensed by the Federal Power Commission as Licensed Project No. 1952-Texas. The project diverts water from the Rio Grande River at river mile 467 by a diversion dam and gravity canal system for irrigation use and for hydroelectric generation at the Central Power and Light Company's Eagle Pass plant. The capacity of the canal is 1,500 second-feet of which 600 second-feet is used for irrigation and 900 second-feet is used for power generation. The installed generating capacity of the hydro plant is 9,600 kilowatts. The plant generation for 1974 was 41,316,000 kilowatt-hours.
The releases from the Amistad Project do affect the operation of the Maverick County Project. Since the capacity of the canal system is 1,500 second-feet, the irrigation and power plant operate most efficiently if the Rio Grande flow above the diversion point is in the 1,500-2,000 second-feet range. We have been advised that in the past the International Boundary and Water Commission has released water from Amistad at widely varying rates.
